'''Sanford Leonard Segal''' ({{Birth date|1937|10|11}} – {{Date of death|2010|5|7}}) was a mathematician and historian of science and mathematics at the [[University of Rochester]]. Mathematically he specialized in [[analytic number theory]], and [[complex analysis]]. He wrote the textbook ''Nine Introductions in Complex Analysis'' (1981), and the [[:wikt:tome|tome]] ''Mathematicians Under the Nazis'' (2003), a historical recount from that period. He also taught courses in [[women's studies]], and [[nuclear arms]]. He was on the Committee of Actuarial Studies at the University of Rochester.<ref>{{cite web |title=OFFICIAL BULLETIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDIES |url=http://www.lib.rochester.edu/IN/RBSCP/Archives_Reg/ATTACHMENTS/1999-2001-UR-Bulletin.pdf |publisher=University of Rochester}}</ref>

==Life==
In 1937 he was born into a conservative Jewish family.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Segal |first1=Sanford |title=Why I Am Not a Christian |url=https://www.friendsjournal.org/2010015/ |website=Friends Journal}}</ref>

In 1958, he received his B.A. degree from [[Wesleyan University]] with Honors in Mathematics and High Honors in Classical Civilization studies.<ref name=retires>{{cite web |title = Sanford Segal retires |publisher = University of Rochester |url = http://www.math.rochester.edu/announcements/Items/2008-Segal-retirement.html |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100514155942/http://www.math.rochester.edu/announcements/Items/2008-Segal-retirement.html |archive-date = 2010-05-14 }}</ref>

In 1959 he spent a year as a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright student]] in [[Mainz]], Germany.

In 1963, he earned his Ph.D. in Mathematics at [[University of Colorado]] under the supervision of [[Sarvadaman Chowla|Sarvadaman D. S. Chowla]] with the dissertation entitled ''The Error Term in the Formula for the Average Value of the Euler Phi Function''.<ref name=ams>{{cite journal |journal = Notices of the AMS |title = Sanford Segal (1937–2010) |publisher = American Mathematical Society |volume = 59 |issue = 9 |author = Allyn Jackson |year = 2010 |page = 1278 }}</ref><ref name=gene>{{MathGenealogy|id=12290}}</ref>

==Career==

After his Ph.D., he worked at the University of Rochester for 44 years until his retirement in 2008. In 1965 he received a grant from the [[Fulbright Program]] as a research fellow in [[Vienna]], Austria. And in 1977, he received a grant from the [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|National Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics]] to teach in [[Rio de Janeiro]].<ref name=retires/><ref name=rochester>{{cite web |url= http://www.rochester.edu/news/show.php?id=3633 |title= Mathematics Professor Emeritus Sanford Segal Dies|last= Blank|first= Alan|date= 24 May 2010|publisher= University of Rochester|access-date=20 November 2012 }}</ref>

In 1981 he published ''Nine Introductions in Complex Analysis'' with North Holland Press (a revised edition was published in 2011 by Elsevier, which had taken over North Holland Press). He later received a grant from [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] to research history of science in [[Nazi Germany]]. [[Princeton University Press]] later published the book ''Mathematicians Under the Nazis'' in 2003,<ref name=retires/> which addresses the experience of mathematics academics in Nazi Germany. The book involved a lot of direct research and interviews with survivors and translations from German.

He translated from French the book ''History of Mathematics: Highways and Byways'' in 2009. In addition, Segal published more than 45 papers on mathematics, [[mathematics education]], and the [[history of science]].

He was a member of the [[Religious Society of Friends]]. He was also a member of [[Sigma Xi]] and of [[Phi Beta Kappa]].

He married Rima Maxwell and had three children, Adam, Joshua, and Zoë.

He died on May 7, 2010.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Inside the AMS | year = 2010 | journal = [[Notices of the AMS]] | volume = 57 | issue = 7 | pages = 892 | access-date = 28 November 2012 | url = http://www.ams.org/notices/201007/rtx100700892p.pdf}}</ref>
